newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* The market players are expected to maintain a defensive stance on continued high interest rates and volatility in Asian currency markets, Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook.

* "Market sentiment will remain sluggish as long as the currency speculation and high interest rates continue....We expect support to be at 2,450 and resistance at 2,700," BPI Securities Corp analyst Roberto Cano said.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index closed slightly lower by 0.11 points at 2,572.69 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 3.49 points lower at 8,113.44. PLDT's ADR closed unchanged at $33.
* The Philippine peso ended steady at 28.47 to a dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 25.03125 percent.
* Damage from the Philippines' de facto devaluation is lkely to be limited because of the country's better economic fundamentals, J.P. Morgan said in a recently published study.

* Philippine President Fidel Ramos will push for passage of a major tax bill and an electoral reform law to prevent poll cheating when he delivers his "Swan Song" at the opening of Congress on Monday, the presidential Palace said.
* Total resources of the Philippine banking system rose 7.3 percent to 2,314.4 billion pesos as of end-March 1997 from the level in December last year, the central bank said on Sunday.

* Philippine money supply growth in July remains restrained, with preliminary data on both base and reserve money showing single-digit growth of nine percent for the first time since May 1996, the central bank said.

* The Philippines can still cope with any challenges against the peso and is on track for continued high growth and low inflation, despite the recent plunge in the currency, President Ramos said Friday night.
* President Ramos has again denied he wants to stay in the top job saying he will not seek another term.
* The Manila Electric Corp said on Friday it posted a 6.6 percent growth in net profits for the first half at 2.53 billion pesos, but analysts said the figure fell below expectations.
* Philippine agriculture and weather experts on Friday said a drought brought on by the El Nino effect could be the worst in years, but measures were underway to mitigate the impact on crops.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Senate ways and means committee approved its version of the remaining component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package (CTRP) last Friday, deciding to lower individual income exemptions, but making sure of a positive fiscal balance.

* Inquirer said quoting Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Perfecto Yasay that the body's prosecution department cleared Philippine Stock Exchange chairman Wilson Sy of alleged insider trading and price manipulation as well as violation of the broker-director rule under the Revised Securities Act.
